The ethylene cracking furnace, which is welded by centrifugal casting heat-resistant steel tubes, is the critical component in petrochemical system.

The specimens were cut from an ethylene cracking furnace tube after a five-year service. The ethylene cracking furnace tubes were exposed at 1223 K– 1373 K with a flowing naphtha at a total pressure close to 0.5 MPa.
The microstructure of as-cast HPNb alloy consists of a cellular γ-matrix and the skeleton shape eutectic carbide
The eutectic chromium carbide of M7C3 with HCP crystalline structure partly transforms to M23C6 with FCC structure
The primary eutectic carbides of M7C3 and NbC will transform into M23C6 and G phase after a long-term high-temperature exposure
The precipitated carbides are M23C6 dispersed in the dendrite interior

evidence.quote: The microstructure of as-cast HPNb alloy consists of a cellular γ-matrix and the skeleton shape eutectic carbide: eutectic carbides on the dendrite boundaries and γ-matrix in grains, which is a typical microstructure of as-cast materials of alloys with high chromium and nickel contents
The primary carbides coarsened and formed a continuous network in the furnace tube after service. The primary carbides width is about 5μm
the secondary carbides with a mean size is approximately 1μm and disperse rather homogenously in dendrite interior

attributes.location: boundary of the matrix and eutectic carbide

evidence.quote: It is a sign of early creep damage that some creep voids appeared at the boundary of the matrix and eutectic carbide.
